items.briefing:
A key theme today for Australian organisations is AI governance. Local research shows Australian executives continue to trust AI systems despite known audit errors, and enterprises are deploying AI agents faster than proper oversight frameworks are in place. This creates real risk — decisions based on flawed AI outputs, or automated systems acting without adequate controls. Separately, a vulnerability in an AI networking tool (OpenClaw) could allow attackers to manipulate AI model behaviour, worth noting if your organisation uses large language model platforms.

On data integrity, Troy Hunt's latest post is a useful reminder to verify data breach claims carefully before acting on them — not every reported breach is legitimate. **Practical tip:** If your team is using AI tools for decisions or reporting, ask how those outputs are being checked for accuracy before anyone acts on them.

featured.title: Australian enterprises are scaling agents faster than governance - MCP is the fix
featured.summary: Governance gaps are slowing enterprise AI adoption, with 79% of Australian DevSecOps professionals saying compliance is getting harder.
